claim: Query results are always sorted by the sort key value; the default order is ascending, and setting ScanIndexForward to false reverses the order.

values.display: ScanIndexForward

evidence.quote: `Query` results are always sorted by the sort key value. If the data type of the sort key is `Number`, the results are returned in numeric order. Otherwise, the results are returned in order of UTF-8 bytes. By default, the sort order is ascending. To reverse the order, set the `ScanIndexForward` parameter to `false`.

claim: A random suffix makes it difficult to read a specific item because the suffix is unknown; a calculated suffix based on something you query on makes single-item reads easier.

evidence.quote: A randomizing strategy can greatly improve write throughput. But it's difficult to read a specific item because you don't know which suffix value was used when writing the item. To make it easier to read individual items, you can use a different strategy.
